thought: A state education board told a blind teenager he couldn't study science. So he sued them - and won.
support: Srikanth Bolla, blind from birth, topped his Class 10 exams, but Andhra Pradesh's board said blind students could only take arts. He challenged the rule in court and won, opening science and maths to every blind student in the state. He then scored 98%, became the first international blind student MIT ever admitted on full aid, and founded Bollant Industries - a company that deliberately hires the people the system once wrote off.
